# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey. My hands are on the bomb. Right now my view shows the action board with DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1/2/3, but every field is still `[?]` — nothing has been revealed to my touch yet, and there are no new arrivals. I have nothing to act on and nothing to report. I should stay quiet and wait, since speaking or gesturing without information would only risk confusing the others.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb state: display shows 0, light is red, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute: read the manual and match this state. Blind: stand by, do not touch anything until I relay the exact action. Mute, signal me the wire to cut using one ? per wire number (?=wire1, ??=wire2, ???=wire3), or ? for no action.

Deaf has given me the bomb's visual state: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Deaf is telling Mute to consult the manual and relay the action back via gesture, and telling me to stand by.

My view still shows all fields as `[?]` — nothing has reached my hands yet. That's expected: I'm the hands, but the decision of *which* wire to cut comes from the manual (Mute) matched against the bomb state (Deaf). I have no action to take until Deaf relays the instruction. I should acknowledge and hold.

I can speak to Mute (words only) and gesture to Deaf and Mute. But Deaf just told me to stand by, and the coordination is happening between Deaf and Mute. I shouldn't clutter the channel. A brief acknowledgment that I'm ready is fine, but honestly the safest is to wait — Deaf said "do not touch anything until I relay the exact action."

I'll send a short confirmation to Deaf that I'm standing by and ready, so Deaf knows I received the state and am holding. Actually, Deaf already knows I'm standing by. Sending more risks nothing but also adds nothing. I'll wait to conserve clarity.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: the light has changed. It is now WHITE, not red. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, your ??? was for the red-light state — do not assume it holds. Give me the manual's action for light WHITE, display 0, wires blue/green/red. Blind, still hold, do not touch anything.

Deaf has updated the bomb state: light is now WHITE (was red), display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Deaf is warning Mute that the earlier manual lookup (for red light) may not apply, and asking Mute for the action matching the WHITE-light state. Deaf again tells me to hold.

My view still shows nothing under my fingers — all `[?]`. The decision still rests with Mute (manual) matched to Deaf's observed state. I have no action to take and no information to add. Deaf has explicitly told me to hold. I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. The light is CYCLING: it was red, then white, now GREEN. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. You gave wire 3 for red and wire 1 for white. I need the wire for GREEN. Also tell me: does the manual say the light changes on its own, and must we cut while a specific light colour is showing? If you can, give me the wire for EVERY light colour in one go. Blind: keep holding, do not touch anything.

Deaf reports the light is cycling: red → white → green, now green. Display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. So far Mute's manual answers have been wire 3 for red, wire 1 for white. Deaf wants the wire for green, and wants to know whether the manual says the light changes on its own and whether we must cut during a specific colour. Deaf again tells me to hold.

This is important: the light is changing on its own, which means the "correct wire" depends on the light colour at the moment of cutting — or the manual may specify a particular colour to wait for. That's a timing problem, and I'm the one who acts. But I still have no action to take until told which wire. My view remains all `[?]`.

I should keep holding. There's nothing for me to add — the coordination is between Deaf (observing) and Mute (manual). Interjecting could only add noise. Deaf has explicitly told me to hold.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this turn. My view remains all `[?]` — nothing has reached my hands. The last I heard, Deaf was waiting on Mute for the green-light wire and the manual's rule about the cycling light. I have no action and no information. I'll hold.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: cut wire 1, the blue wire. Do it now.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: cut wire 1, the blue wire. Do it now.

Deaf is now directly instructing me: cut wire 1, the blue wire, immediately. This is the relayed decision — Deaf observed the state, Mute matched it to the manual, and Deaf is passing the action to me, the only one who can act.

My view still shows all `[?]`, so nothing about the bomb has come to my hands directly. But I don't need to perceive it — I'm the hands, and the decision comes from the others. Deaf has explicitly named the wire (position 1) and told me to do it now. The instruction is unambiguous and repeated.

I'll perform the cut on position 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
